summary: Grounded audit of galpy backend code for jit-fast / backend-specific speedup opportunities (no internal jit), ranked into a roadmap

items.title: Roll bisect_root's fixed for-loop into lax.while_loop (jax) with a static trip count, threaded from callers
items.mechanism: jax-specific rewrite of `for _ in range(n)` (optimize.py:165) to jax.lax.while_loop with a data-independent iteration cap as the cond (sign-preserving carry, branch-free xp.where body), so the body traces ONCE instead of unrolling 100 copies; torch keeps the eager Python loop; numpy unchanged (scipy.optimize.brentq). Also thread an explicit static nsteps=/width-hint through bisect_root so n_bisect_steps does not fall back to maxiter=100 under tracing (verified: traced probe -> 100 vs concrete ~46-51); Staeckel callers pass maxiter=200, doubling that segment again.
items.why_ranked_here: Single highest reach in the codebase: bisect_root is the ONE shared kernel behind backend brentq, consumed by Potential.rl/rE/zmaxgrid/rliftedgrid, actionAngleSpherical rperi/rap, actionAngleVertical xmax, actionAngleIsochroneInverse eta, and twice per Staeckel turning-point solve. Each call bakes ~100 (Staeckel: 200) unrolled physics-closure f-evaluations into the compiled graph. Rolling once is the named-lever class and fixes every consumer at once.

items.title: Roll the Staeckel/Spherical/Vertical expanding-bracket loops into lax.while_loop/fori_loop (jax)
items.mechanism: jax-specific rewrite of the fixed-count Python for-loops in the turning-point finders to lax.while_loop/fori_loop with a static cap; the body is already a single branch-free xp.where update so it ports directly. numpy stays on the eager loop (byte-identical; numpy does not unroll a graph).
items.why_ranked_here: Concrete instances of the named 47k-equation-jaxpr lever in the hottest AA subsystem. _staeckel_uminumax (60+80) + _staeckel_vmin (80) bake ~220 full _JRStaeckelIntegrandSquared/_JzStaeckelIntegrandSquared (-> potentialStaeckel) evals into the graph BEFORE the two bisect_root calls; Spherical (2x80) and Vertical (80) mirror it. Highest per-subsystem compile lever after the shared bisect_root, stacks with P0#1.

items.title: Collapse c_stm_forward's 6-per-IC variational integrations into ONE stacked integrate_dxdv call
items.mechanism: Replace the inner `for i in range(6)` (fresh Orbit + integrate_dxdv per basis column) with a single integrate_dxdv propagating all 6 canonical deviation vectors as 6 stacked copies, exactly the Lyapunov idiom Orbits.py:2893-2907 (Orbit(numpy.repeat(vxvv,6)) + integrate_dxdv(eye-stack, rectIn=True, rectOut=True, numcores=...)), reshape to (N,nt,6,6). Integrates the base orbit ONCE (bit-identical across columns), collapses 6 dispatches to 1, parallelizes columns over numcores.
items.why_ranked_here: ~6x forward-cost reduction on the fast-C STM gradient path (the headline differentiable IC-gradient route); the optimal pattern is already proven in-repo (Lyapunov, rectIn/rectOut=True) and supported by integrateFullOrbit_dxdv ([N,6], numcores). Broad reach -- every jax/torch C-STM gradient and routed dop853_c integrate from a backend IC pays the 6x today -- and the reference implementation already exists, low risk.
locations: galpy/backend/_reference/inbackend_stm.py:59-83 (for ic / for i in range(6); base re-integrated all 6)

items.title: Vectorize the EllipsoidalPotential GL node loop (_potInt / _forceInt_all / _2ndDerivInt_all)
items.mechanism: Replace per-node `for k in range(len(glx))` with a single broadcast over a node axis: form m of shape (...,K) using glx as an array, call dens(m)/psi(m) ONCE on batched m, multiply by glw, reduce with one xp.sum(axis=-1). glx/glw are static leggauss constants (fixed K), so one fused op replaces K unrolled iterations each spawning its own dens()/sqrt()/where().
items.why_ranked_here: Universal inner loop for every PerfectEllipsoid/TwoPowerTriaxial/PowerTriaxial force/Hessian eval; glorder~20-50 means K unrolled integrand copies in the graph + K eager dispatches warm. Collapses to 1 dispatch and shrinks the graph ~K-fold for the dominant cost term, all four regimes. P1 not P0 only because reach is one potential family vs the cross-cutting root-finder.

items.title: Add combined force / Hessian evaluators so the backend path stops recomputing the expansion 3x/6x per point
items.mechanism: Expose a single _all_cyl_forces returning (FR,Fz,Fphitorque) from ONE _compute_*_forces_at_point call, and a combined Hessian evaluator returning all six cyl 2nd-deriv components from the one 8-tuple the chain rule already derives. numpy shares via the md5 _force_hash / _2nd_deriv_cache_key caches, disabled for jax/torch (trace-hostile), so the backend recomputes the full (N,L,M) SCF expansion / GL quadrature 3x (forces) and 6x (Hessian) at the same point. Have inbackend_ode._eom_rhs use the combined force evaluator.
items.why_ranked_here: 3-6x redundant expansion/quadrature on the heaviest per-point kernels (SCF Legendre+Gegenbauer, Multipole tables, Ellipsoidal GL), amplified by inbackend_ode._eom_rhs issuing all three force calls every adaptive ODE stage. Broad reach across SCF/Multipole/Ellipsoidal and both differentiable paths.
locations: galpy/potential/EllipsoidalPotential.py:226-229,291-301 (hash cache guarded by `if xp is numpy`)

items.title: Gate the C-STM forward on requires-grad so a no-gradient backend-IC integrate skips the 6x variational solve
items.mechanism: jax custom_vjp primal _stm calls a base-orbit-only host fn; only _fwd (when differentiating) computes M. For torch, detect requires_grad in _CSTMFunction.forward and skip the STM assembly + save_for_backward when not needed. Combined with P0#3 a forward-only integrate drops from 6 variational integrations to one base integration.
items.why_ranked_here: Orbits.py:1748 routes ANY 6D backend-IC orbit with a dxdv C method through _integrate_cstm, so users wanting only a backend-array trajectory silently pay ~6-7x. Broad (every non-differentiated backend-IC integrate), but depends on P0#3 landing first to realize the base-only saving.
locations: galpy/backend/_jax/orbit_stm.py:29-49 (_host/_stm always compute M, primal discards it)

items.title: Replace streamdf's 6-point finite-difference AA Jacobian (calcaAJac) with analytical jacfwd, and batch the per-chunk track loop
items.mechanism: calcaAJac approximates the 9x6 d(J,Omega,angle)/d(x,v) by forward differences (dxv=1e-8, mod-pi turning-point guard); replace with jax.jacfwd/torch.func.jacfwd of the now-traceable Staeckel actionsFreqsAngles -- exact, removes the 6-call FD loop. Separately batch the `for ii in range(nTrackChunks)` track loop by stacking all chunk base-points + FD perturbations into ONE batched aA call. FLAGGED: jacfwd is NOT byte-identical to the FD result -- gate behind the backend resolver, keep FD for numpy.
items.why_ranked_here: Track assembly is THE setup cost of streamdf/streamgapdf (~7*nChunks*(1+nIter) serial scalar Staeckel AA evals, default nChunks 20-60). jacfwd removes the 6x FD multiplier AND gives exact derivatives, unlocking the differentiable stream-fit gradient w.r.t. potential params -- the headline backend use case. L effort + depends on batched-AA + needs review for the non-byte-identical numpy divergence, so P1 not P0.

items.title: Hoist the single _staeckel_jacobian call and share the 6 derivative panels between _staeckel_freqs and _staeckel_angles
items.mechanism: Lift the one _staeckel_jacobian call (12 t^2-substituted derivative-panel quadratures + detA + Omegas) into _staeckel_actions_freqs_angles and pass the six derivatives (and detsafe/Omegas) into BOTH consumers instead of each recomputing them. Pure backend-agnostic refactor; numpy byte-identical.
items.why_ranked_here: Verified: _staeckel_freqs (line 320) and _staeckel_angles (line 388) BOTH call _staeckel_jacobian and the full path invokes both, so the 12-quadrature derivative computation runs TWICE per orbit -- a clean ~2x halving of the dominant cost after turning points across all four regimes. Low risk, M effort, compounds with the turning-point loop rolls.

items.title: Add a native batch axis to the in-backend diffrax/torchdiffeq ODE so N orbits integrate in one solve
items.mechanism: Thread a leading batch axis through _eom_rhs/_to_eom/_from_eom (the force layer is already elementwise in R,z,phi, so vmapping the RHS is natural) so diffrax/torchdiffeq integrate a stacked (N,6) state in one adaptive solve, avoiding an outer vmap of the whole diffeqsolve (which re-traces/recompiles per N and gives N independent step sequences).
items.why_ranked_here: The in-backend ODE path is the parameter-gradient / higher-order-diff path whose point is GPU-batch training loops; single-orbit-only is the difference between a usable GPU pipeline and one bottlenecked on per-orbit dispatch. High impact for GPU-large-N, but L effort and narrower regime reach than the P0 levers.

items.title: Rewrite assoc_legendre's O(L*M) Bonnet recurrence as a lax.scan over l, with vectorized derivative tables
items.mechanism: The l-recurrence (P[l][m] from P[l-1],P[l-2]) is the only loop-carried part -> one lax.scan over l carrying (P_{l-1},P_{l-2}) for all m at once, collapsing the L*M list-of-lists + 2-level nested xp.stack into one carried buffer. The deriv=1/2 loops read only the finished P table -> ONE vectorized elementwise map over the (L,M) grid, not per-cell xp.where. jax-specific kernel; keep the list+stack Python path as torch/numpy-trace fallback.
items.why_ranked_here: Largest unrolled graph in the special-fn subsystem, on the SCF/Multipole force path (SCFPotential.py:456,760,890; MultipoleExpansionPotential.py:2549); deriv=2 emits ~3*L*M separately-traced ops + a nested stack at L,M~10-30. Same ~12x-class compile win. L effort, algebraically constrained, partly subsumed if the combined-evaluator (P1) lands.

items.title: Vectorize the gegenbauer L-call comprehension + N-step recurrence and share the C^a/C^{a+1}/C^{a+2} family per SCF point
items.mechanism: (a) Fold alpha (affine in l) into a leading (L,)-axis and run ONE lax.scan over n carrying (C_{n-1},C_n) for all L alphas, collapsing the `xp.stack([gegenbauer(N,alpha(ll),xi) for ll in Ls])` L*N unroll to N scan steps. (b) Compute the family C^a/C^{a+1}/C^{a+2} once per point and pass it to _phiTilde/_dphiTilde/_d2phiTilde instead of each re-calling _C/_dC/_d2C on the same xi (~3x forces, ~6x Hessian).
items.why_ranked_here: SCF radial basis is evaluated on every SCF force/density call; L*N unroll + 3-6x family recompute bloat the SCF graph and warm cost. Strong overlap with the combined force/Hessian evaluator (P1), scoped medium, natural companion to assoc_legendre sharing the scan idiom.

items.title: custom_jvp for the Staeckel/spherical/vertical action integrals using the existing analytical Leibniz dJ integrands
items.mechanism: Attach jax.custom_jvp / torch.autograd.Function to J(E,Lz,I3) whose tangent uses the already-implemented derivative panels (djrdE/djrdLz/djrdI3 from _staeckel_jacobian; spherical/vertical radial-period integrands). Forward value stays the plain sqrt-GL quadrature (byte parity); the backward pass skips differentiating through xp.sqrt(clip(S)) at near-turning-point nodes (sqrt'(0)=inf) and decouples the gradient from the node count.
items.why_ranked_here: Exact, well-conditioned, cheap action gradients (galpy already has the dJ integrands), but gradient-regime-only with no warm-forward change, L effort. Lower reach than the compile-time loop rolls; the streamdf jacfwd (P1) is the higher-leverage gradient consumer.

items.title: Cache GL node/weight tables as backend arrays per (xp, n, device) in _gl01_on
items.mechanism: gauss_legendre_01 caches only numpy float64 tables; _gl01_on runs asarray_on_device(xp, x01, dev) on EVERY fixed_quad/transformed_quad/nested_quad call -- a fresh host->backend materialization (host->device on GPU) of the same constant grid. Add a dict cache keyed by (id(xp), n, device-key). Warm-only (under jit the constant folds); numpy short-circuits to the cached numpy tuple (byte-identical).
items.why_ranked_here: Cross-cutting (one cache helps Staeckel 3 calls/eval, Vertical 3, Spherical, Potential.mass, qdf, SCF nested_quad) and only S effort, but warm-path-only and folds away under jit, so it does not touch the dominant compile blowup.

items.title: Share per-node S(u),S(v) evaluations across the 3 factor integrands in the Staeckel angle/jacobian panels
items.mechanism: PE/PI/PL, QE/QI/QL, and the six _staeckel_jacobian panels call the helper 3x with the same Sfunc/nodes, differing only by factor_fn. Refactor to evaluate 1/sqrt(S) once on the node grid and return all three weighted sums (factor as a cheap elementwise multiply), turning 3 node-grids into 1 per branch.
items.why_ranked_here: ~3x cut in angle/jacobian node-potential evals, compounds with the freqs/angles jacobian de-dup (P1). Backend-agnostic, byte-identical. P2 because it is finer-grained sharing already addressed coarsely by the P1 jacobian hoist; do after that to avoid churn.

items.title: Share node potential evals across the spherical Or/Op/angler/anglez panels (fuse azimuthal/non-azimuthal pairs)
items.mechanism: The azimuthal vs non-azimuthal panel over the SAME limits differ only by a 1/r^2 factor on identical nodes; collapse each pair into one node-radicand evaluation returning both moments, and return Or/Op to the angle helpers so panels are not recomputed. Reduces ~8 n-node grids to ~4-5.
items.why_ranked_here: Cuts a substantial fraction of spherical angle-path potential sampling, backend-agnostic, but one AA family of medium reach; sequence after the spherical bracket-loop roll (P0#2) and combined-force work to avoid overlapping edits.

items.title: Fuse the per-RHS-step force dispatch into one pass over _potlist and hoist isDissipative out of the step loop
items.mechanism: _eom_rhs does 3 separate Python dispatches into _evaluateRforces/_evaluatephitorques/_evaluatezforces, each re-iterating a CompositePotential's _potlist with a per-component isDissipative branch (3 full passes/step). Compute all three components per component in one loop reusing R,cosphi,sinphi and the isDissipative branch once; precompute the (dissipative-mask, component-list) once per integrate.
items.why_ranked_here: torchdiffeq runs the field eagerly every adaptive step so the 3x redundant dispatch + isDissipative re-checks are pure per-step overhead; for diffrax it enlarges the traced RHS. Real but constant-factor, largely subsumed by the P1 combined-force evaluator.

items.title: Thread diffrax potential parameters as diffeqsolve args (not a closed-over Python object) and shrink max_steps
items.mechanism: diffeqsolve closes over the Python pot object (trace keyed on its pytree/identity) with an empty args slot and static max_steps=100000 (sizes internal while-loop buffers). Thread the potential's array-valued parameters through diffeqsolve args so re-using the same structure with new values reuses the compiled solve (and makes parameter-gradients first-class), and derive a smaller max_steps from len(ts).
items.why_ranked_here: Directly helps the fitting-loop case (params change every step -> recompile if closed-over), jax-only and needs a parameter-pytree plumbing design; sequence after the native batch axis (P1) which touches the same RHS.
locations: galpy/backend/_jax/orbit_ode.py:19-32 (pot closed over, args unused, max_steps=100000)

items.title: Reduce the STM VJP residual from full (N,nt,6,6) to the adjoint-needed (N,6) by contracting over t host-side
items.mechanism: The VJP residual is the full STM M of shape (N,nt,6,6); backward only needs sum_t M(t)^T ct[t]. Push the t-contraction into the host callback (or store smaller per-time pieces) so the saved-tensor / host<->device transfer drops from O(N*nt*36) to O(N*36) for the IC gradient.
items.why_ranked_here: Helps gradient-regime memory pressure and large-batch GPU training for long output grids, but the forward cost dominates the fast-C STM path so this is a memory/transfer optimization not a FLOP win; do after P0#3 and P1 STM-gating land.

items.title: Batch the constantbetadf.fE / sphericaldf._dMdE per-energy quadrature comprehensions into fixed 2D GL tensor evaluations
items.mechanism: fE evaluates quadpack.quadrature TWICE per energy in a Python comprehension over ~202 energies; anisotropic _dMdE runs a doubly-nested per-energy quad. Build (nE,nGL[,nGL]) GL node grids mapped to each energy's interval (inner L-limit closed-form), evaluate the already-vmappable integrand ONCE on the flattened grid, contract with weights. numpy byte-identical.
items.why_ranked_here: Removes 400+ adaptive-quadrature subgraphs from DF setup (constantbetadf is jax-only -> direct payoff), but these are setup/diagnostic methods not hot inner loops, narrower reach than streamdf track assembly (P1).

items.title: Batch streamgapdf impulse per-star Orbit integration into one stacked-Orbit integrate
items.mechanism: Replace `for i in range(nstar): Orbit([...single...]).integrate(...)` (+ flipped reverse) with a single Orbit(numpy.array([R,vR,vp,z,vz,phi]).T) integrating all stars in one call (and the reverse arm together), as streamspraydf._sample_tail:596-598 already does; index o.x(times) as (nstar,nt). Lets the in-backend ODE integrator batch all trajectories.
items.why_ranked_here: Large CPU win and the exact batch-of-trajectories pattern the new ODE integrator is built for, reference batched pattern already in streamspraydf, but the analytical kick path (not this loop) is the default fast route, so impact medium and reach one DF method.

items.title: Cache per-(device,dtype) special-fn series/node tables (hyp2f1/bessel_k/sici) and add a positive-only torch gamma fast path
items.mechanism: (a) hyp2f1/k0/k1/kn/sici re-asarray their numpy GL/trapezoid/Laguerre constants to device every call -- add a per-(namespace,device,dtype) memo (subsumed by the shared _gl01_on cache where applicable). (b) torch gamma_fallback always evaluates the reflection branch even for positive args (Einasto/PowerSphericalwCutoff) -- add a positive-only fast path; refresh _NATIVE_MISSING against current torch.special capability.
items.why_ranked_here: Warm-only per-call constant-factor + smaller AD graph; folds away under jit. S effort, low individual impact, cheap hygiene that compounds with the shared _gl01_on cache -- bundle with that work.

items.title: Batch the umin/umax bisections into one [2,N] solve reusing already-computed bracket f-values
items.mechanism: umin and umax are two roots of the SAME f bracketing ux from below/above via two separate bisect_root calls; stack the two brackets along a leading axis and call bisect_root ONCE on the batched [2,N] bracket (one vectorised f per step), and reuse the f(ux+/-eps)/f(lo)/f(hi) already computed for the at_turn/reaches_axis logic instead of recomputing inside the bisections.
items.why_ranked_here: Halves the separate root solves + per-op launches for the u turning points, stackable with the bisect_root lax roll (P0#1) -- but once bisect_root is a single traced while_loop the marginal win shrinks, so do after P0#1 to size the remaining benefit. vmin is a single root so only u benefits.

shared_wins: Roll the shared bisect_root for-loop (optimize.py:165) into lax.while_loop ONCE -> shrinks the traced graph for EVERY backend root-find consumer simultaneously: Potential.rl/rE/zmaxgrid/rliftedgrid, actionAngleSpherical rperi/rap, actionAngleVertical xmax, actionAngleIsochroneInverse eta, and the two per-Staeckel-turning-point calls. The single broadest-reach item in the roadmap.

Thread a static bisection step count (or width hint) through bisect_root so n_bisect_steps stops falling back to maxiter=100 under a tracer (verified: traced probe -> 100 vs concrete ~46-51; Staeckel passes maxiter=200) -> roughly halves the iteration count of every backend bisection under jit and warm, compounding with the while_loop roll. S effort, all consumers.

Add a per-(xp, n, device) cache for GL node/weight tables in _gl01_on (quadrature.py:213) -> one fix removes a per-call host->device node-table transfer for every quadrature consumer (Staeckel actions/freqs/angles, Vertical, Spherical, Potential.mass, qdf, SCF nested_quad) and subsumes the special-fn hyp2f1/bessel_k/sici per-call table re-uploads.

Introduce combined force (FR,Fz,Fphitorque) and combined Hessian (all six cyl components) evaluators -> one pattern eliminates the backend-path 3x force / 6x Hessian recompute across SCF, Multipole AND Ellipsoidal at once (their numpy md5/key caches are all disabled for jax/torch) and directly de-bloats inbackend_ode._eom_rhs (the most-executed differentiable code, calling all three force evaluators per ODE stage).

Establish the lax.scan-over-a-loop-carried-recurrence + vectorize-the-non-carried-derivative-tables idiom ONCE (assoc_legendre) and reuse it for gegenbauer and any future Bonnet/3-term recurrence; both sit on the SCF/Multipole hot path and are the special-fn instances of the named 47k-jaxpr/12x-compile lever.

Reuse the in-repo stacked single-call integrate_dxdv pattern (already proven in the Lyapunov path Orbits.py:2893-2907 with rectIn/rectOut=True) for BOTH the c_stm_forward 6-column collapse and the streamgapdf per-star impulse batching -> the same idiom fixes redundant base-orbit integration in two subsystems.

Make the in-backend ODE RHS (_eom_rhs) batch-capable AND fused-force in one coordinated edit -> the leading-batch-axis (orbit-integration P1) and the single-pass-over-_potlist fuse (P2) touch the same RHS/force layer, so design them together to avoid churn; both also enable the streamgapdf batched-Orbit and any GPU training pipeline.
rejected: No audit proposed an internal jax.jit / torch.compile call inside galpy -- all high/medium items use jit-COMPATIBLE rewrites (lax.while_loop/fori_loop/scan for control flow, custom_jvp/custom_vjp for gradients, broadcast+sum vectorization for GL node loops). Nothing violated the no-internal-jit rule, so nothing was dropped on that ground.

numpy-only ndindex per-point loops in SCF/Multipole expansion assembly (SCFPotential.py:515-518; SphericalHarmonicPotentialMixin.py:74-83,218-221; MultipoleExpansionPotential.py:1615-1650): vectorizing them changes numpy reduction order and breaks byte-identity, and touches NEITHER the jit nor the gradient path -- low value and policy-flagged. Keep as a numpy-only lever surfaced for the user's explicit review, not part of the backend roadmap.

EllipsoidalPotential(glorder=None) scipy.integrate.quad and FerrersPotential scipy.quad + numpy.roots fallbacks (EllipsoidalPotential.py:462-464; FerrersPotential.py:397,475): a backend-traceability COVERAGE gap (these triaxial routes don't work under jax/torch at all), not a speedup on an already-working path; L-effort rewrite of unmigrated code. Track as a correctness/coverage item, not a performance opportunity here.

iv/kn integer-order upward recurrences (bessel_i.py:45-46; bessel_k.py:102-103): loop-carried but galpy's only consumer is RazorThinExponentialDisk._R2deriv at n=2, so the loop unrolls to ~1 step -- negligible graph cost. Listed in the audit only for recursion-audit completeness; not worth a scan rewrite.

jax pure_callback STM per-(N,nt)-shape re-specialization + host round-trip (orbit_stm.py:17-44): the C integrator is inherently a host call so the device round-trip is structural, not a bug; the only realistic win is shape-bucketing/padding for variable-length time grids, and most training loops use a fixed batch size. Low impact; fold into documentation/guidance rather than a code change.

transformed_quad two-panel integrand fusion (quadrature.py:431,436) and get_namespace memoization (~0.7-3.2us/call, _resolver.py:27-53): both real but low-ceiling (panel count fixed at 2; per-call resolve folds away under jit and is dwarfed by the loop-unroll items). Defer indefinitely unless profiling of a specific warm-eager pipeline flags them.

streamdf spread eigen-decomposition / slerp per-chunk loops (streamdf.py:1054-1101,1569-1611): O(nChunks) tiny 2x2/6x6 linalg ops -- the warm win is modest and the jit-traceability benefit is small relative to the heavy AA-carrying loops in the same file. Low priority; revisit only after the track-assembly AA batching (P1) lands.

isochrone actionAngle (closed-form, no quadrature/root-find) and quasiisothermaldf vmomentdensity (already vectorizes its ngl^3 GL grid into one batched self() call; residual cost is the action eval, owned by the action-angle subsystem) -- no opportunity. diskdf/evolveddiskdf are legacy 2D solar-neighborhood DFs unlikely in GPU/gradient pipelines; interpRZPotential is not backend-migrated (scipy splines), out of scope.
roadmap.narrative: The four audits converge on one dominant theme: galpy's backend paths are full of Python for-loops and redundant recomputes that, while correct, bake giant subgraphs into the user's jit/grad trace and pay 3-6x redundant work warm because the numpy md5/key caches are deliberately disabled for jax/torch. The single broadest lever is the shared bisect_root for-loop (optimize.py:165), whose n_bisect_steps falls back to 100 iterations under a tracer (verified) and which sits behind EVERY backend root-find -- Staeckel/Spherical/Vertical turning points, Potential.rl/rE/zmax/rgrid, IsochroneInverse -- so rolling it once into lax.while_loop (jax) shrinks the graph for all of them simultaneously. Stacked on top are the explicit expanding-bracket loops (Staeckel 60+80+80, Spherical 2x80, Vertical 80) and the special-fn recurrences (assoc_legendre O(L*M), gegenbauer L*N), the concrete instances of the named 47k-equation-jaxpr / ~12x-compile lever in the hottest subsystems. The second pillar is redundant recompute on the backend path: c_stm_forward re-integrates the identical base orbit 6 times when the Lyapunov code already proves a single stacked integrate_dxdv works, the EllipsoidalPotential GL quadratures unroll K~20-50 node iterations that vectorize to one batched dens(m)+sum, and the disabled force/Hessian caches mean 3x/6x recompute of the SCF/Multipole/Ellipsoidal expansions per point -- amplified because inbackend_ode._eom_rhs calls all three force evaluators every ODE stage. The gradient regime gets two clean wins: custom_jvp on the action integrals using galpy's existing analytical Leibniz dJ integrands, and replacing streamdf's 6-point finite-difference AA Jacobian with jacfwd (exact, 6x fewer evals, unlocks differentiable stream fitting). Recommended first moves: (1) roll bisect_root into lax.while_loop and thread a static step count -- one change, every consumer benefits; (2) collapse c_stm_forward to a single stacked integrate_dxdv and gate the STM on requires-grad; (3) vectorize the EllipsoidalPotential GL node loop and the assoc_legendre/gegenbauer recurrences. All proposals respect no-internal-jit and keep numpy byte-identical via the existing scipy/eager fallbacks.

opportunities.title: Replace unrolled fixed-count bracket + bisection loops with lax.while_loop (jax) / tensor-while (torch) in the Staeckel/spherical/vertical turning-point finders

audits.summary: The action-angle backend path (Staeckel vectorised core + spherical/vertical mirrors; isochrone is already closed-form with no quadrature/root-find, so no opportunity) has two dominant, named-lever-class problems. (1) UNROLLED LOOPS: the turning-point finders run fixed-count Python for-loops (60/80 expanding-bracket halvings + bisect_root's up-to-200 bisection steps, which under a jit tracer always fall back to the 200-step worst case via n_bisect_steps), each iteration calling a full _evaluatePotentials -> ~550+ unrolled potential evals per Staeckel orbit just for the J_R turning points, the action-angle analog of the 47k-equation Staeckel jaxpr; lax.while_loop/fori_loop (jax) and tensor-while (torch) collapse the body to one trace (high, compile+gradient). (2) REDUNDANT RECOMPUTE: _staeckel_actions_freqs_angles calls both _staeckel_freqs and _staeckel_angles, each independently re-running _staeckel_jacobian's 12 derivative-panel quadratures (a clean ~2x halving, high); within those panels the 3 factor integrands (PE/PI/PL, QE/QI/QL, and the 6 jacobian panels) re-evaluate the same Sfunc/potential on identical nodes ~3x (medium); and the spherical Or/Op/angler/anglez path samples the potential on ~8 separate n-node grids, several differing only by a 1/r^2 weight on identical nodes (medium). A gradient-regime lever: the action integrals autodiff through xp.sqrt(clip(S)) at near-turning-point nodes (ill-conditioned), while galpy already has the exact analytical Leibniz dJ integrands -> a custom_jvp gives cheap, well-conditioned action gradients (medium). Smaller levers: batch the umin/umax bisections into one solve and reuse already-computed bracket f-values (medium); thread a static bisection step count to avoid the 200-step tracer fallback (low). All findings respect no-internal-jit (jit-COMPATIBLE rewrites: lax control flow, custom_jvp, fusion -- no internal jit/compile); numpy paths stay byte-identical via the existing scipy/eager fallbacks.

audits.summary:
The orbit-integration subsystem has two distinct differentiable paths: a fast C state-transition-matrix path (inbackend_stm.py + _jax/_torch orbit_stm.py, IC gradients only) and a backend-agnostic diffrax/torchdiffeq ODE path (inbackend_ode.py + orbit_ode.py, parameter + higher-order gradients). The highest-value wins are structural, not jitting (all findings respect no-internal-jit):

(1) THE big one — c_stm_forward (inbackend_stm.py:57-83) does 6 separate Orbit()+integrate_dxdv calls per IC, each redundantly re-integrating the identical base orbit, when integrateFullOrbit_dxdv already supports propagating all 6 basis vectors in ONE vectorized C call (the Lyapunov code in Orbits.py:2893-2907 already uses exactly this stacked single-call idiom with rectIn/rectOut=True). ~6x forward cost.

(2) Both STM wrappers always compute the full 6-column STM even for a no-gradient forward integrate, and ANY 6D backend-IC orbit is routed through this path (Orbits.py:1748) — so plain trajectory integration on a jax/torch IC silently pays 6-7x. Gate the variational solve on requires-grad.

(3) The diffrax/torchdiffeq ODE path is single-orbit only (_eom_rhs/_to_eom assume a flat (6,) state); N-orbit GPU/training use is forced through an outer vmap that re-traces per N and can't share adaptive steps — add a native batch axis.

(4) The VJP residual is the full (N,nt,6,6) STM (large host<->device transfer for long time grids).

Lower-tier: per-RHS-step Python dispatch is 3x redundant (separate R/phi/z evaluators each re-iterating _potlist with per-component isDissipative branches — torchdiffeq runs this eagerly every adaptive step), the diffrax solve closes over the Python potential object (recompiles per potential instance; max_steps=100000 inflates compiled buffers) rather than threading parameters as diffeqsolve args, the jax pure_callback re-specializes per (N,nt) shape, and per-step isDissipative lookups should be hoisted out of the step loop.

audits.summary: The special-functions subsystem (Pspecial router + _fallback/) is already correctly native-preferring and the numpy path is byte-identical, so the real levers are the pure-backend fallbacks that contain Python loops which UNROLL under a user's jax.jit. Two findings are high-value and clearly worth doing: (1) assoc_legendre's triple nested O(L*M) Bonnet recurrence (assoc_legendre.py:37-94) is the largest unrolled graph in the subsystem and sits on the SCF/Multipole force path (deriv=2 => ~3*L*M separately-traced ops + a 2-level nested stack); its l-recurrence is a textbook lax.scan and its derivative tables (deriv=1/2) are NOT loop-carried and should be ONE vectorized map, not per-cell xp.where loops. (2) gegenbauer is called L times inside an SCF Python comprehension (SCFPotential.py:1059), each running an N-term loop-carried recurrence, for an L*N unroll that folds to N scan-steps if alpha is vectorized over an L-axis. Both are backend-SPECIFIC jax kernels (keep the existing list+stack as the torch/numpy-trace fallback) and respect no-internal-jit (they make the code traceable/cheap-to-compile, they do not call jit). Medium-value: node/series tables (GL 128-node for hyp2f1, trapezoid/Laguerre for k0/k1/sici) are re-uploaded to device every call because gauss_legendre_01 caches only numpy constants -- add a per-(device,dtype) memo (warm-CPU/GPU win, S effort, backend-agnostic); and the torch gamma_fallback always evaluates the reflection branch even for positive arguments, inflating the warm path and AD graph for Einasto/PowerSphericalwCutoff. The iv/kn upward recurrences are loop-carried but n is tiny (2), so low impact -- listed only so the recursion audit is complete. The series/quadrature `for k` loops in hyp2f1/sici/k01 are fixed small counts already vectorized over the data and are not worth changing. Nothing here requires violating the no-internal-jit rule.

opportunities.title: streamdf track assembly: batch the per-chunk action-angle Jacobian instead of a Python chunk loop of scalar AA calls
opportunities.mechanism: fuse-vectorize: replace the `for ii in range(self._nTrackChunks)` loop (executed once + nTrackIterations times) with a single batched call. Each chunk calls _determine_stream_track_single -> aA.actionsFreqsAngles(scalar) once + calcaAJac which does a 6-point forward-difference Jacobian = 6 MORE scalar aA.actionsFreqsAngles calls (calcaAJac:4144). So per chunk = 7 scalar AA evals; with the default nTrackChunks=floor(deltaAngleTrack/0.15)+1 (often 20-60) and up to 2 iterations that is ~7*nChunks*(1+nIter) = hundreds of scalar AA evaluations. Stack all chunk base-points + their 6 finite-difference perturbations into one (nChunks*7, 6) array and evaluate aA.actionsFreqsAngles ONCE on the whole batch (the vectorized Staeckel AA at afa0aa8b/HEAD is now jit-traceable and batch-capable), then reshape to form all Jacobians with numpy/xp ops. This both removes the eager per-chunk dispatch AND, under user j.jit, collapses the unrolled chunk loop into one batched AA graph.
opportunities.impact_rationale: Track assembly is THE setup cost of streamdf/streamgapdf and dominates instantiation; it is O(nChunks * nIter) scalar AA evaluations (each AA eval is itself expensive Staeckel quadrature). Batching to one AA call gives near-linear speedup in nChunks on CPU (fewer Python/dispatch round-trips) and is the only way GPU action-angle batching can help here. Re-fitting a stream for a likelihood scan re-runs this every call.

opportunities.mechanism: custom_vjp/custom_jvp-analytical: calcaAJac currently approximates the 9x6 Jacobian d(jr,lz,jz,Or,Ophi,Oz,ar,aphi,az)/d(R,vR,vT,z,vz,phi) by forward finite differences with dxv=1e-8 (4115) and the modulo-pi turning-point guard (4170). It also unlocks differentiable stream fitting (gradient of the track w.r.t. potential params), the headline use case for the backend project.

audits.summary: The df-streams hotspots cluster into two backend-relevant categories. (1) STREAMDF TRACK ASSEMBLY is the dominant target: track setup runs a Python `for ii in range(nTrackChunks)` loop (streamdf.py:1257, repeated nTrackIterations times at 1309), and each chunk calls calcaAJac (4136), which itself does a 6-point finite-difference Jacobian = 6 extra scalar aA.actionsFreqsAngles calls. That is ~7*nChunks*(1+nIter) serial scalar Staeckel action-angle evaluations per stream. The two highest-value fixes are (a) BATCH all chunk base-points + FD perturbations into one vectorized AA call (now possible since the vectorized Staeckel AA was made jit-traceable at HEAD afa0aa8b), and (b) replace the finite-difference Jacobian with an ANALYTICAL jacfwd of the traceable AA (custom_jvp) — exact, 6x fewer evals, and it unlocks the differentiable stream-fit gradient that is the headline use case. (2) NESTED-QUADRATURE SETUP in sphericaldf/constantbetadf: per-energy `for tE in ...` quadrature list comprehensions (constantbetadf.fE:363/390 two quads each over ~202 energies; sphericaldf anisotropic _dMdE:899-921 doubly-nested quad; isotropic _dMdE:805) and per-radius spline-build loops (_make_pvr_interpolator:659, _setup_rphi_interpolator:727) all collapse to batched fixed Gauss-Legendre tensor evaluations over a flattened grid. Secondary: streamgapdf impulse kicks integrate one Orbit per star in a Python loop (1729, 1831) — batchable to a single stacked-Orbit integration exactly like streamspraydf already does (596-598), ideal for the new in-backend ODE integrator. NONE of the proposals require internal jit; all keep the numpy path byte-identical as a fallback. NOTE for user review: the streamdf jacfwd substitution replaces a 1e-8 forward-difference Jacobian (calcaAJac:4115/4150-4178, including its mod-pi turning-point guard) with exact AD derivatives — this is NOT byte-identical to the numpy FD result and must be gated behind the backend resolver with the FD path preserved for numpy. Quasiisothermaldf's GL vmomentdensity (640-830) and diskdf/evolveddiskdf were reviewed and are NOT prioritized: qdf already vectorizes its ngl^3 GL grid into one batched self() call (the residual cost is the action evaluation, owned by the actionAngle subsystem), and diskdf/evolveddiskdf are legacy 2D solar-neighborhood DFs unlikely to appear in GPU/gradient pipelines.

The infrastructure subsystem's dominant, cross-cutting performance problem is unrolled Python for-loops in the shared root-finder and its AA consumers, which bake giant subgraphs into the user's jit/grad trace. The single highest-value lever is bisect_root's `for _ in range(n)` (optimize.py:165): n_bisect_steps falls back to 100 iterations under tracing (verified empirically -- traced probe returns 100 vs concrete ~46-51), so EVERY backend brentq call (Potential.rl/rE/zmax/rgrid, actionAngleSpherical/Vertical/IsochroneInverse) unrolls 100 copies of a physics closure into the graph; rolling it once into lax.while_loop (jax) helps all of them. The same antipattern recurs as explicit expanding-bracket loops in actionAngleStaeckel (60+80+80 potentialStaeckel evals at lines 127/133/164), actionAngleSpherical (two range(80) at 564/569), and actionAngleVertical (range(80) at 336) -- these are the concrete instances of the known 47k-equation-jaxpr / ~12x-compile lever in the hottest AA subsystem. All of these respect the no-internal-jit rule: they make galpy jit-COMPATIBLE via lax control flow with static trip counts, never jitting internally, and keep the numpy path byte-identical (it still dispatches to scipy / stays eager). Secondary warm-path/GPU wins: _gl01_on re-materializes the cached GL node tables to backend arrays on every quadrature call (quadrature.py:215 -- a repeated host->device transfer for the shared fixed_quad kernel behind Staeckel/Vertical/Spherical/mass/qdf/SCF), a tighter static bisection cap, fusing transformed_quad's two integrand calls, and memoizing get_namespace's per-call array_namespace dispatch (~0.7-3.2us, 724 call sites). Note: backend/linalg.py does not exist in this tree (linalg lives in backend/interpolate.py's spline solves, outside the named scope and not a hot lever).
